stories.title: Anthropic launches its IPO roadshow at $70-$78 a share, implying a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
stories.summary:
Anthropic launched the roadshow for its initial public offering and set a price range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion at the top of the range.

- The range lands well above recent reports that its expected valuation had fallen from as high as $2 trillion to about $1 trillion
- The public S-1 shows soaring revenue and enterprise adoption alongside heavy losses (about $8 billion last year, per Engadget)
- The seven co-founders get a combined 50.1% of the vote on most matters, and each plans to sell the same number of shares, about $250M apiece at the midpoint, while keeping control
- Amazon is set to make far more from the IPO than Anthropic's VC backers, and the SpaceXAI deal is bigger than previously known
- Risk factors warn that Anthropic's own AI could pose an existential risk, and Blackstone expects credit agencies to rate it high "junk" after listing, per the FT

stories.title: Meta's Muse comes to Apple Watch and Wear OS as it passes 10M users amid mounting controversies
stories.summary:
Meta's Muse, a personal AI agent built on its Muse Spark model platform, keeps adding features and users even as privacy, security, content, and labor controversies mount.

- New: Muse is now on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS, where users can talk to it through voice calls, text messages, or dictation (TechCrunch)
- Recent features include Spaces for collaborating with the agent, avatar video chat for US users, and a planned Tamagotchi-like Muse wearable
- Meta said on its Q3 earnings call that Muse has over 10 million users; Zuckerberg said a quarter of them shop through the agent, spending about $200 per purchase on average
- Meta suspended Muse's conversation sharing after researchers showed shared links exposed sensitive personal and business data
- Other controversies: OnlyFans creators object to Muse's sexual chat, a since-fixed Mac 0-day, and a contractor "human concierge" reportedly making racist remarks on calls
- Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com; Meta admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw

- Nvidia stock slid more than 4% after the probe opened; one law firm has filed a proposed investor class action and others have announced investigations

stories.title: Tech rout wipes out $2.5 trillion as AI investors brace for scrutiny from incoming Democrats
stories.summary: Tech stocks plunged, erasing about $2.5 trillion in value, on fears that incoming Democrats will end the Trump era of laissez-faire regulation and backdoor deals that AI companies have benefited from, Gizmodo reports.
